candidates.title: IRL Flex: Backlash Against Self-Optimization Culture
candidates.shift: Marketing-trend data suggests consumer fatigue with 'maxxing'/self-optimization and AI-generated content, replaced by demand for unpolished, in-person ('IRL flex') experiences and 'spend to feel' purchases.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if optimization fatigue is real, retailers and venue operators may need to invest in tactile, imperfect, human-staffed physical spaces rather than frictionless digital/AI experiences to keep shoppers engaged.
candidates.evidence: Global Wellness Summit's 'over-optimization backlash' piece; Digiday stat that preference for AI-made creator content fell from 60% to 26%; Time article on looksmaxxing scoring apps.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of consumer culture pivoting from digital self-optimization toward valorizing physical, imperfect, in-person experience; if it holds, brands and venue operators would need to redesign retail/hospitality spaces around authenticity and tactility rather than algorithmic polish.
candidates.author: Florian Schleicher

candidates.title: The Confidant Gap: Rising Share of Americans With No One to Talk To
candidates.shift: Survey data indicates a growing share of Americans lack a spouse, close friend, or coworker to confide in during hard times, deepening the loneliness epidemic.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: sustained isolation could increase demand for informal 'third places' — cafés, libraries, community centers, faith spaces — as substitute support infrastructure, reshaping how such spaces are funded and staffed.
candidates.evidence: Pew's American Trends Panel 142 data via the Association of Religion Data Archives; cited Harvard loneliness-epidemic research.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of eroding informal social infrastructure — from dense interpersonal support networks to isolated individuals — driven by declining civic/religious participation and changing work/family patterns; if it continues, physical third-places may need to formalize a support-network role they weren't originally designed for.
candidates.author: Ryan Burge

candidates.title: AI Purchasing Agents Trigger Merchant Lockouts
candidates.shift: Personal AI agents (Meta's Muse, Instinct) now transact and book on users' behalf at machine speed; Resy deactivated an account after an automated assistant made 200+ requests per hour.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: this is a concrete early flashpoint where booking/reservation platforms, restaurants, and retailers must engineer against bot-driven demand spikes — capacity planning, rate-limiting, and fraud/abuse policy may need rapid redesign.
candidates.evidence: Inc. report on Resy deactivating a user after an AI assistant made 200+ requests/hour; Meta's Muse agent launch; Wired coverage of Walmart-OpenAI agentic shopping deal.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of the transaction interface shifting from human-paced browsing to machine-paced agentic requests; the Resy lockout is an early operational collision that shows physical-world service systems (reservations, inventory, staffing) were not built for non-human request volumes and may need new throttling/verification infrastructure.
candidates.author: Mike Mallazzo

candidates.title: Fifty-Year Decline in Weekly Worship Attendance
candidates.shift: GSS longitudinal data shows US weekly-or-more religious attendance fell from 41% (1972) to ~25% (2024), while never-attenders rose from 9% to 30%.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: sustained decline implies growing structural surplus of underused sanctuary/assembly space, likely accelerating adaptive reuse, deconsecration, and conversion of religious buildings to housing, offices, or community facilities.
candidates.evidence: General Social Survey trend data (1972-2024) presented with multiple charts; author's ongoing Religious Behavior Index series.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a decades-long secularization trend moving from majority regular attendance to majority non-attendance, driven by generational replacement and declining institutional belonging; if it continues, a large share of US religious real estate stock will need repurposing, with implications for local zoning, historic preservation, and community-space supply.
candidates.author: Ryan Burge
